t.template.what: Controls the visual layout and design style of each frame (title, text, image arrangement)
t.template.how:
Place .html template files in templates/SIZE/ directories (e.g., templates/1080x1920/). Templates are automatically grouped by size. Custom CSS styles are supported.

**Template Naming Convention**

- `static_*.html` → Static style templates (no AI-generated media)
- `image_*.html` → Image generation templates (AI-generated images)
- `video_*.html` → Video generation templates (AI-generated videos)

**Note**

At least one of the following browsers must be installed on your computer for proper operation:
1. Google Chrome (Windows, macOS)
2. Chromium Browser (Linux)
3. Microsoft Edge

t.storyboard.generation.explanation.title: Settings guide
t.storyboard.generation.explanation.body:
**Smart**: AI reads the full script first, then plans which text each shot covers. Best for most topics.

**By Any Punctuation (Chinese/English)**: Splits at commas, periods, question marks, and other punctuation, but preserves `%` and `《》` when they belong to the text.

**By Sentence-End Punctuation (。.!?！？)**: Splits only where sentences end, giving steadier pacing.

**Auto**: AI chooses a suitable count from the configured storyboard range. **Scenes**: manually set the exact storyboard frame count for Smart mode.

**Max storyboard frames**: In both deterministic modes, the default is 60. You can raise it only up to the current deployment cap, and that deployment cap can never exceed 200. If your environment sets a lower cap, the slider stops there.

**max_tokens**: This controls how much JSON the model may output in Smart mode. It is not the storyboard frame count.

**Note**: If deterministic splitting still creates more segments than your selected max storyboard frames, the system will report an error. Consider increasing the max within the deployment cap, switching to Smart mode, or shortening the input text.

t.ip_design.intro.title: 🎭 Welcome to IP Design Workbench
t.ip_design.intro.what_is_ip_body: IP (Intellectual Property Character) refers to virtual characters or personas that appear repeatedly in videos. Through IP design, you can maintain character consistency across multiple videos and create unique brand characters.
t.ip_design.intro.concept_asset_bible_body: AssetBible is a container for IP assets, similar to a project folder. It contains multiple IP Profiles (character designs), scenes, props, and style definitions. A project can have multiple AssetBibles, such as 'Cartoon Characters', 'Realistic Portraits'.
t.ip_design.intro.concept_ip_profile_body: IP Profile defines the complete characteristics of a specific character, including: visual anchors (features that must be preserved), adaptable items (features that can change with scenes), role capabilities (types of roles the character can play), etc.
t.ip_design.intro.concept_scene_cast_body: SceneCast binds IP characters to specific storyboard frames. It tells the system: in this shot, which character to use, what scene, what props, and what style.
t.ip_design.intro.concept_visual_anchors_b: Visual anchors are core features that the character must maintain, such as 'pink hair', 'blue eyes', 'round face'. These features never change across any scenes and are key to maintaining character consistency.
t.ip_design.intro.concept_adaptable_body: Adaptable items allow AI to freely adjust features based on the scene, such as 'clothing color', 'accessories', 'expressions'. Properly setting adaptable items helps characters blend naturally into different scenes.
t.ip_design.intro.quick_start_step1: 1. Fill in an ID in the AssetBible section below (e.g., my_character)
t.ip_design.intro.quick_start_step2: 2. Switch to the 'IP Profile' tab and fill in character information
t.ip_design.intro.quick_start_step3: 3. Click 'Save AssetBible' to save your design
t.ip_design.intro.quick_start_step4: 4. Go back to Home, enable your IP in the 'IP Character Integration' section

t.ip_design.guide.title: 📖 IP Design Guide
t.ip_design.guide.what_is_ip_body: The IP (Intellectual Property Character) Design Workbench is the core tool for creating and managing video IP characters. By defining the character's appearance, identity anchors, adaptable items, and presence rules, AI can maintain character consistency across video generations.
t.ip_design.guide.step1_body: AssetBible is the container for IP assets. First, fill in the AssetBible ID at the top, then switch to the IP Profile tab to fill in the IP's basic information and visual anchors.
t.ip_design.guide.step2_body: Enter the IP name, logline, visual summary, and other core information. The visual summary is the most important input for the LLM — describe the character's appearance, clothing, and features in detail. Identity locks are key to maintaining character consistency.
t.ip_design.guide.step3_title: ③ Configure Visual Anchors & Adaptable Items
t.ip_design.guide.step3_body: Identity locks (e.g., hair color, face shape) tell the LLM which features must be preserved. Adaptable items (e.g., clothing color) allow the LLM to adjust freely based on the scene. Balancing these ensures both consistency and flexibility.
t.ip_design.guide.step4_body: In the Scene Cast tab, bind characters, scenes, props, and styles to specific storyboard frames. Each SceneCast represents a complete casting plan for one storyboard frame.
t.ip_design.guide.step5_body: Go back to the Home page, enable IP in the IP Character Integration section, and select the created AssetBible and IP Profile. AI will automatically maintain character consistency during video generation. You can also apply SceneCast per-frame in the Storyboard Workbench.
t.ip_design.guide.best_practice1: The more detailed the visual summary, the better the character consistency. Include: hairstyle, hair color, face shape, eye color, clothing style, body type.
t.ip_design.guide.best_practice2: Don't overuse identity locks (3-5 is ideal), or the AI will lack creative room.
t.ip_design.guide.best_practice3: First-time users can import built-in AssetBibles from the Presets tab to quickly get hands-on experience.
t.ip_design.guide.best_practice4: Use the Readiness tab to check if your IP meets the requirements for generation.

t.selfhost.warning.message:
1. First, **load and run** `{workflow_path}` workflow in your ComfyUI environment ({comfyui_url})
2. Ensure the workflow **runs successfully** without missing nodes or models
3. After the workflow is verified, return to this project to use it

t.render_backend.label: Render backend
t.render_backend.help: Choose which rendering path this task should use.

t.render_backend.caption.hyperframes_compi: Uses the new compiled HyperFrames path for rollout testing.
t.render_backend.caption.ffmpeg_manifest: Uses a manifest-driven FFmpeg path for simple image, video, audio, ASS, and overlay composition.
t.caption_style.title: Caption Style
t.caption_rendering.enabled_help: Render bottom captions in the final video. On by default.
t.caption_style.font_family_help: Place font files under the project-root fonts/ directory (preferred). font/ and resource/fonts/ are also checked. The dropdown uses the font file's internal family name when available, for example Noto Sans CJK SC; if it does not take effect, confirm the internal family name matches this value.

The dropdown uses the font file's internal family name when available, for example Noto Sans CJK SC; if it does not take effect, confirm the internal family name matches this value.

t.text_rendering_preview.title: Instant preview
t.text_rendering_preview.instant_notice: Updates immediately from the selected template, size, media placement, and text styles.
t.text_rendering_preview.real_stale: Real preview frame is stale. Generate it again.

t.text_layer.title: Overlay Text Layer
t.text_layer.enabled_help: Render planned words after image generation instead of relying on the image model to draw text.
t.image_text.suppress_embedded_text_help: When enabled, the prompt below is appended to image generation prompts to avoid visible Chinese, English, subtitles, watermarks, and other embedded text.
t.image_text.positive_prompt_help: This text is appended to the positive image prompt when embedded-text suppression is enabled.
t.tts_audio_strategy.label: TTS audio strategy
t.tts_audio_strategy.help: Choose whether narration is generated per frame or prepared as a master track first.
t.tts_audio_strategy.caption.auto: Auto keeps local legacy on per-frame audio and switches ComfyUI-backed legacy jobs to master-track preparation.
t.tts_audio_strategy.caption.per_frame: Generate narration separately for each frame.
t.tts_audio_strategy.caption.master_track: Generate narration as a master track first, then derive frame clips from it.
t.element_animation.enabled_help: Segment generated images into foreground elements and add subtle animation.
t.tts_split_mode.label: TTS split mode
t.tts_split_mode.help: Long text uses the appropriate internal or external segmentation strategy for the selected TTS workflow.
t.tts_split_mode.caption.internal_only: Pass complete text to the selected TTS workflow and let the model handle segmentation internally.
t.tts_split_mode.caption.external_only: Pixelle splits by budget and punctuation before TTS, useful for compatibility paths that need explicit audio boundary control.
t.tts_text_policy.preserve_natural_punctua: Only affects the narration-generation prompt; caption display formatting stays separate.
t.tts_text_policy.joiner_mode_help: Controls whether spaces are inserted when multiple speech units are merged for TTS.
t.tts_text_policy.caption_punctuation_mode: Only affects displayed captions, not the text sent to TTS.
t.article_concretization.enabled_help: Turn article judgments, structures, or causal relationships into explainable diagram imagery.
t.article_concretization.diagram_aspect_ra: Controls the diagram panel's own ratio; static templates may keep layout fixed.
When a static template does not allow layout changes, the diagram panel ratio cannot be adjusted.
t.article_concretization.diagram_approved_: Separate labels with commas, Chinese commas, enumeration commas, or line breaks.
t.article_concretization.diagram_user_inte: Add the relationship, conflict, or explanation direction the diagram should emphasize.
t.storyboard.enabled_help: Turn on preset-driven planning controls and optional frame overrides.
t.storyboard.advanced_enabled_help: Turn on preset-driven advanced planning controls and optional frame overrides.
t.storyboard.advanced_not_enabled_hint: Enable to stabilize visual style, shot language, and role consistency through presets. Generate once, then lock fields you want to keep in the Storyboard Workbench.
t.storyboard.world_preset_enabled_help: When checked, a preset world scene is used to stabilize visual style, prop systems, and role identities. Leave unchecked to let the AI work without world constraints.
t.storyboard.generation_world_hint_help: Describe the current script world, narrative boundaries, and how the IP should fit this generation. This does not overwrite the IP design world hint.
t.storyboard.generation_world_hint_missing: Fill in the script before generating a world hint draft.
The selected IP has no default world hint.
t.storyboard.prompt_language_help: Controls the language used by storyboard planning fields and generated image prompts.
t.storyboard.preset.world.neutral_knowledg: A clean, restrained explainer space with whiteboard, reference props, and simple classroom or lab staging. The safest default when you want clarity without strong stylistic packaging.
t.storyboard.preset.world.dual_mode_storyb: A versatile scene that switches between concept explainer and theme mapping. Comparison boards and reusable teaching props support stable output across varied topics.
t.storyboard.preset.world.angry_birds_thre: Faction banners, strategy boards, war maps, encampments, and scrolls build a dramatic stage for historical figures, faction dynamics, and character rivalries.
t.storyboard.preset.world.angry_birds_know: A bright, playful classroom with teaching boards, demo tables, labeled samples, and charts. Ideal for general science, life tips, and recurring explainer series.
t.storyboard.preset.world.angry_birds_hist: A history narrative space with timeline walls, archive shelves, a lecture podium, historical maps, and artifact stands. Built for biographies, dynastic shifts, and factual walkthroughs.
t.storyboard.preset.shot.balanced_explaine: A balanced teaching rhythm that covers both setup and detail, keeping the lesson pacing even.
t.storyboard.preset.shot.detail_focus.name: Detail Focus
t.storyboard.preset.shot.detail_focus.desc: A shot preset that emphasizes key details and tighter framing for important cues.
t.storyboard.preset.shot.opening_world_bui: An opening-heavy shot preset that establishes world context before tightening into teaching beats.
t.storyboard.preset.shot.character_relatio: A shot preset that keeps people, factions, and comparisons readable together across the batch.
t.storyboard.preset.shot.classroom_demo.de: A classroom-style shot preset built around medium frames and demonstration pacing.
t.storyboard.guide.default_on_title: Storyboard planning stays on by default
t.storyboard.guide.default_on_body: When storyboard planning is enabled, the planner uses preset continuity, shot language, and role mapping by default. Start with the built-in presets, then tighten locking only if the result still drifts.
t.storyboard.guide.when_to_turn_off.title: When to turn it off first
t.storyboard.guide.when_to_turn_off.body: Turn it off while you are still exploring rough direction, validating prompts, or adjusting an unstable outline. That keeps iteration faster and removes constraints until the structure settles.
t.storyboard.guide.title: How to use storyboard planning
t.storyboard.guide.combo.explainer.title: Stable explainer baseline
t.storyboard.guide.combo.explainer.body: Keep the default world preset, use Balanced Explainer, leave content mode and role strategy on auto, and only raise role locking to Strong when the presenter identity keeps drifting.
t.storyboard.guide.combo.theme_mapping.bod: Switch content mode and role strategy to Theme mapping when each frame should translate the same idea into a visual motif. If you want the framing rhythm to follow the preset more strictly, change shot strategy to Strict.
t.storyboard.guide.combo.iteration.title: Fast direction finding
t.storyboard.guide.combo.iteration.body: Leave most settings on default, keep consistency on Standard, and keep shot strategy Adaptive. This gives the planner enough structure without making early exploration feel boxed in.
t.storyboard.guide.field.world_preset: Sets the world identity, continuity anchors, and the default relationship between subject and setting. Pick the world that best matches the overall tone first.
t.storyboard.guide.field.shot_preset: Shapes shot rhythm, framing bias, and the style of explanation. Think of it as the camera-language template for the whole batch.
t.storyboard.guide.field.consistency_stren: Controls how hard the planner pushes continuity. Standard keeps more variety; Strong trades variety for stability.
t.storyboard.guide.field.content_mode: Tells the planner whether this batch behaves more like a concept explainer or a theme-mapping exercise. Auto is the safest default when you are unsure.
t.storyboard.guide.field.role_strategy: Decides whether roles are inferred automatically, held as a stable explainer cast, or mapped from themes into visual characters.
t.storyboard.guide.field.role_locking_stre: Only changes how firmly role identity is preserved across frames. Raise it when faces, outfits, or casting logic keep shifting.
t.storyboard.guide.field.shot_strategy: Adaptive leaves more room for generation creativity. Strict keeps the result closer to the preset shot design.
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker_title: How to choose world and shot presets
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.world.tit: World preset: decide which universe is carrying the lesson
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.world.bod: World presets define reusable role flavor, recurring props, background motifs, and the overall packaging of the lesson. Start from the subject matter, then choose the world that should carry it.
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.world.ite: The safest default. A clean, restrained explainer space — best for general concept breakdowns when you do not want strong stylistic packaging yet.
Useful when the topic is still exploratory and may switch between concept explanation and theme mapping. More flexible than Clean Classroom, but intentionally less opinionated as a scene.

Best for Three Kingdoms topics, faction rivalries, character relationships, and history-to-character mapping. The core is faction banners, strategy maps, scrolls, and a dramatic stage — slot your source figures into the theater.
Best for life science, physics principles, and general knowledge explainers. A bright classroom with a stable presenter and teaching props, suitable for recurring explainer series.
Best for history events, biographies, timelines, and factual walkthroughs. Leans into podiums, archive shelves, historical maps, and timeline walls as the signature narrative space.
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.shot.titl: Shot preset: decide how this batch should be filmed
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.shot.body: Shot presets control distance mix, pacing, and emphasis. Think of them as the storyboard grammar for the batch, not the art style of a single frame.
t.storyboard.guide.preset_picker.shot.item: The default all-rounder. It balances wide, medium, and tight framing well and is the safest starting point for most explainer videos.
Use this when local structure, props, experiments, or key details need to read clearly. It intentionally spends more time in tighter framing.
Use this when the opening should first establish the world, setting, or cast relationships clearly. It starts wider, then tightens as the lesson focuses.
Use this when comparisons, factions, role contrast, or character relationships are central, such as Three Kingdoms dynamics, branded cast contrast, or teacher-student interaction.
Use this for classroom demonstrations, step-by-step teaching, or presenter-led examples. It favors medium teaching coverage with selective close detail inserts.
t.storyboard.guide.override_title: What to do after one generation
t.storyboard.guide.override_body: Generate once, then open the Workbench page in the left navigation to review the storyboard and lock the fields you want to preserve. The next run will keep those locked values while still allowing other parts to improve.
t.storyboard.preview.title: Preview overrides
t.storyboard.preview.help: Lock the frame fields you want to keep on the next generation.
t.storyboard.preview.empty: Generate once to inspect the latest storyboard planning snapshot here.

t.storyboard.workbench.open_hint: Storyboard preview, field locks, and dependency state now live in the Workbench page.

t.series_visual_signature.presentation.cap: Product-level policy that preserves the visual signature while preventing advanced option conflicts from failing the whole generation.
t.series_visual_signature.presentation.vis: Visible supporting character in every frame

Recommended: repair only failed frames, preserve successful frames, and record fallback reasons.
